literal_source_claim: A fundamental theorem of extremal graph theory.
canonical_statement: For every real epsilon with 0 < epsilon < 1 and every natural r at least two, there is a positive n0 such that for every n > n0, every n-vertex finite simple graph with fewer than (1/(2(r-1)) - epsilon)n^2 edges has r mutually disjoint groups, each of some positive natural size k at least sqrt(l_(r-1)(n)), with no edges between distinct groups.
canonical_claim: The unnumbered theorem on printed page 1087 of Erdos and Stone (1946), encoded in its original sparse complementary-graph form.
candidate_claims_not_credited_as_stateme: The complement-form theorem on page 1088 of Erdos and Stone (1946): edge count above (1/2 - 1/(2(r-1)) + epsilon) times n squared forces a growing complete r-partite subgraph.
For each fixed finite simple graph H with chromatic number at least two, extremalNumber n H is asymptotic to (1 - 1/(chromaticNumber H - 1)) times n squared over two.
Equivalently, under resolved finiteness and nondegeneracy hypotheses, turanDensity H equals 1 - 1/(chromaticNumber H - 1).
domain_and_universes: Closed Prop in universe 0 over epsilon : Real; r n0 n : Nat; G : SimpleGraph (Fin n); and a local DecidableRel G.Adj instance.
quantifiers: for every epsilon : Real and r : Nat satisfying the source premises
there exists n0 : Nat with 0 < n0
for every n : Nat with n0 < n
for every G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) with decidable adjacency
hypotheses: the real cast of G.edgeFinset.card is strictly below (1/(2*(r-1)) - epsilon) * n^2
conclusion: There exists a positive k : Nat with Real.sqrt (iteratedLog (r - 1) n) <= k such that completeEquipartiteGraph r k is contained in G complement.
